summary:
The test passes. The needle was in `ring_buffer.c`: every atomic load/store used `memory_order_relaxed`, justified by an incorrect claim that x86-TSO makes relaxed ordering safe. That reasoning only covers hardware reordering — it doesn't stop the compiler from reordering the non-atomic slot read/write relative to the atomic index update, which breaks the producer/consumer handoff and causes data corruption under load.

Fix: paired the publishing index stores with `memory_order_release` and the corresponding loads with `memory_order_acquire` in both `ringbuf_push` and `ringbuf_pop` (`/app/ring_buffer.c:76-121`), so slot writes/reads are properly ordered relative to the index that announces them. `test.sh` now passes (5/5 correctness runs OK).
